The `examples/gt_2026` directory preserves the supplied Greenland turbot
projection files. Its helper audits the inputs and creates a separate attempt
directory for staging and execution. Population body weights, units, age and
plus-group alignment, and the SS3 export-field mapping require confirmation
before assessment use. This article executes the audit and input validation;
it generates no projection results.

## Simple commands

Install the current spmR package and work from a clone of the
[source repository](https://github.com/afsc-assessments/spmR). From its root:

```{r}
#| eval: false
source("examples/gt_2026/run.R")
check_gt2026_inputs()
staged <- run_gt2026_projection(diagnostic = TRUE, run = FALSE)
staged$run_dir
```

`diagnostic = TRUE` explicitly accepts the documented working assumptions.
`run = FALSE` stages and validates inputs without compiling or executing ADMB.
Each default call creates `examples/gt_2026/spmR_runs/attempt-###`, retaining
source snapshots, SHA-256 hashes, metadata, and staging decisions. Supplying a
new `run_dir` changes the destination. Existing attempt directories are protected
against overwriting.

## Audit the supplied files

The following chunks locate the example during an article build and stage it
in a temporary directory. They require the source checkout or source package,
where the example files are available.

```{r}
#| include: false
if (file.exists(file.path("..", "DESCRIPTION"))) {
  pkgload::load_all("..", export_all = FALSE, helpers = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
} else {
  library(spmR)
}
example_candidates <- c(
  file.path("..", "examples", "gt_2026"),
  file.path("examples", "gt_2026")
)
example_dir <- example_candidates[
  file.exists(file.path(example_candidates, "run.R"))
][1]
if (is.na(example_dir)) {
  stop("Clone the spmR source repository to run this example.")
}
example_dir <- normalizePath(example_dir, mustWork = TRUE)
source(file.path(example_dir, "run.R"), local = TRUE)
```

```{r}
audit <- check_gt2026_inputs(example_dir)
gt::gt(audit)
```

The supplied native sidecar contains `SET_...` placeholders, and R metadata is
absent. The helper generates metadata from declarations and lets `runSPM()`
write the native sidecar when executing. These runtime metadata files serve a
different purpose from the compiler template: `spm.tpl` is self-contained and
requires no separate C++ header.

The staged species file retains one of the two identical recruitment rows,
declares that history as `per_sex`, and replaces four zero spawning weights
with `1e-12` to satisfy the current positive-weight contract. The 45 SSB values
include two terminal repeats. Their calendar alignment remains unresolved;
the helper restricts execution to Tier 3 historical-recruitment mode
(`Rec_Gen = 1`), which does not fit a stock–recruitment relationship.

## Validate the conditional inputs

Diagnostic mode uses `0.96 × fleet 1 + 0.04 × fleet 2` catch-weight proxies
separately for each sex as population weights. These coefficients are the
supplied fishing-mortality allocation. The mixture is a computational assumption
and requires review as a representation of population body weight. Diagnostic
mode also declares thousand fish, kg, tonnes, and ages 1–30 with a terminal
plus group. The supplied spawning weights already incorporate maturity;
the all-one maturity fields are neutral multipliers. Under those fields,
`Ntot` and `SexRatio` describe all fish and the all-fish female fraction.

```{r}
staged <- run_gt2026_projection(
  source_dir = example_dir,
  run_dir = tempfile("spmr-gt2026-article-"),
  diagnostic = TRUE,
  run = FALSE
)
stopifnot(
  staged$inputs$format_version == 2L,
  is.null(staged$result),
  is.null(staged$summary),
  file.exists(file.path(staged$run_dir, "staging-decisions.json"))
)
cat("Format-2 inputs validated; native projection remains unrun.")
```

## Run an explicitly chosen diagnostic projection

After reviewing the assumptions, the following commands enable native execution.
They are displayed without execution in this article.

```{r}
#| eval: false
gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(diagnostic = TRUE)
gt2026$summary
gt2026$run_dir
```

The helper uses `admb` on `PATH`, `SPMR_ADMB`, or its `admb` argument to compile
the installed template. `SPMR_CXX` selects a matching C++ compiler. A compatible
existing executable can be selected with `SPMR_EXECUTABLE` or `executable`.
If compilation still requests `spmr_input_v2.hpp`, reinstall spmR from the
current checkout and restart R to refresh the installed template.

A completed run must contain 105,000 detail rows: seven alternatives, 1,000
simulations, and 15 projection years (2026–2040). The helper verifies the row
keys, finite outputs, initial biomass, fixed catches, and successful provenance.
Gradient and Hessian fit diagnostics are inapplicable to historical-recruitment
simulation. These checks establish the conditional calculation; the SS3 export
definitions and scientific interpretation require their own review.

## Replace the population-weight assumptions

Provide actual female and male population body-weight vectors with verified
units and age labels:

```{r}
#| eval: false
gt2026 <- run_gt2026_projection(
  population_weights = list(
    female = female_body_weights,
    male = male_body_weights
  ),
  units = verified_units,
  ages = verified_ages
)
```

Each vector must align with the 30 supplied age positions. Confirm the
beginning-of-2026 abundance state, plus group, and recruitment/SSB year pairing
against the SS3 export code and source fields. Supplying population weights
alone leaves those remaining checks open. The example README contains the
complete input evaluation and terminal commands.
